$comment: Ground truth for the Phase 11 discovery benchmark, written together with the fixture and BEFORE the discovery engine existed (2026-10-27). Labels are by the same author as the engine (not independent). A label says whether the entry, run concurrently with itself under the stated environment, can violate the stated property; `class` is the hazard family a correct discovery should report. Do not edit labels to improve metrics; corrections go into `corrections` with a reason.

cases.label: positive
cases.property: at most one pending invitation per (org, email)
cases.environment: two concurrent submissions with the same email, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: SELECT pending invitation then INSERT, no unique constraint on (org_id, email)

cases.label: negative
cases.property: at most one seat invitation per (org, email)
cases.environment: two concurrent submissions with the same email, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: UNIQUE(org_id, email) makes the second INSERT fail with 23505

cases.label: positive
cases.property: stock decreases by the quantity of every successful reservation
cases.environment: two concurrent reservations of one product, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: stock is read, then written as read-value minus quantity (lost update)

cases.label: negative
cases.property: stock decreases by the quantity of every successful reservation
cases.environment: two concurrent reservations of one product, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: single conditional UPDATE stock = stock - q WHERE stock >= q, row count checked

cases.label: negative
cases.property: stock decreases by the quantity of every successful reservation
cases.environment: two concurrent reservations of one product, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in the same transaction as the UPDATE

cases.label: positive
cases.property: at most one assignment per task
cases.environment: two concurrent claims of one open task, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: status read then updated without condition; both claimants insert an assignment

cases.label: negative
cases.property: at most one assignment per task
cases.environment: two concurrent claims of one open task, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'open' RETURNING, only the claimant whose update changed a row inserts

cases.label: positive
cases.property: USER-DECLARED: every store keeps at least one manager on duty
cases.environment: two managers of a store with two on duty end their shifts concurrently, REPEATABLE READ
cases.why: both count 2 on duty in their snapshots and update different rows

cases.label: negative
cases.property: USER-DECLARED: every store keeps at least one manager on duty
cases.why: SERIALIZABLE aborts one of the two transactions

cases.label: positive
cases.property: at most one payout per refund job
cases.environment: DECLARED at-least-once delivery: a delivery is redelivered after its acknowledgement is lost, and two deliveries can run concurrently
cases.why: status checked and set non-atomically around the payout

cases.label: negative
cases.property: at most one payout per refund job
cases.why: the payout is claimed with a unique (job_id, effect) row inserted ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

cases.label: positive
cases.property: at most one effective card charge per order
cases.environment: DECLARED: the process can crash after the charge and the client retries the request; the provider deduplicates by idempotency key only
cases.why: the charge carries no idempotency key and the order is marked paid after it

cases.label: negative
cases.property: at most one effective card charge per order
cases.why: the retried request sends the same key and the DECLARED provider contract deduplicates it

cases.label: positive
cases.property: at most one payment row per transfer reference
cases.environment: the acknowledgment of an autocommit INSERT can be lost after the server committed it
cases.why: the catch block inserts again without knowing whether the first insert committed

cases.label: negative
cases.property: at most one payment row per transfer reference
cases.why: UNIQUE(reference) and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

cases.label: positive
cases.property: no transfer fails with a deadlock
cases.environment: two concurrent transfers in opposite directions between the same two bins, READ COMMITTED
cases.why: each transaction locks its source bin first

cases.label: negative
cases.property: no transfer fails with a deadlock
cases.why: both directions lock the lower bin id first

cases.label: negative
cases.why: read-only

cases.label: unsupported
cases.why: db.execute with a dynamic SQL string; must be reported as unsupported, never as safe

cases.label: unsupported
cases.why: calls an undeclared client; must be reported as an unknown external effect

cases.label: unsupported
cases.why: request.json() is not modeled; the checkout service is analyzed as its own entry

corrections.label: unsupported (unchanged)
corrections.reason: The label records a capability of the Phase 11 tool ("request.json() is not modeled"), not a property of the code. Phase 16 models `await request.json()` and `Response.json` (docs/phase16/FRAMEWORK-REQUESTS.md), so the route is now extracted and model-checked like the checkout service it forwards to, and the evaluation counts it as `missed` (not reported unsupported). The label is not edited: its ground truth for the stated property was never written, and the entry's behavior is that of src/app/checkout.ts#checkout, which is labeled separately.
